newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end at record high, Skandia jumps.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end at record high, Skandia jumps.

text.p: 1500 GMT - Swedish shares rose to end at a record high on Monday, supported by U.S. Friday gains and blue chips advancing.
* Stockholm general index up 0.23 percent to a record high of 2,875.42
* Trade was quiet as markets in the U.S. and Britain were closed and turnover was a modest 3.23 billion crowns.

* Insurer Skandia kept performing strongly, up eight crowns to 293 after rocketing 34 crowns on Friday. The share benefited from analysts upgrading the value of the group's U.S. unit linked division, AFS.
Swedish shares rose to end at a record high on Monday, supported by U.S. Friday gains.
"I think we have seen the highest level this week," an analyst said. "The large fall in France on Monday could affect the Stockholm bourse on Tuesday."

The Stockholm bourse's general index rose 0.23 percent to a record high of 2,875.42. Trade was quiet as markets in the U.S. and Britain were closed and turnover amounted to a modest 3.23 billion crowns.
Insurer Skandia kept gaining, up eight crowns to 293 after rocketing 34 crowns on Friday.
The share benefited from analysts upgrading the value of the group's U.S. unit linked division AFS.
Automotive group Volvo jumped 4.5 crowns to 214 ahead of a redemption. Some players also mentioned a rebound.

"This is a recovery compared to the other large companies," an analysts said. "In addition, there have been many positive figures for Volvo lately such as new car and truck sales. Volvo's situation in the U.S. also looks somewhat better."
Car safety equipment group Autoliv showed its muscles and rose 4.5 crowns to 304.5 and metals and mining group Trelleborg advanced two crowns to 139.5.
Trelleborg was boosted by favourable newspaper reports about the listing of its Boliden mining unit in Toronto.
Telecoms group Ericsson came off day highs to close lower, down 1.5 crowns to 277.5.
Drugs major Astra gained 2.2 crowns to 134 after a bonus issue of one share for three and a split of two for one. Analysts expected the share to keep moving upwards.
